photos.question: The nurse is giving iron dextran by intramuscular injection. Which technique is correct?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #343!

💉 This injection technique keeps iron from staining the skin!

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Use the Z-track method

🧠 Rationale: Iron dextran can stain the skin and irritate tissue.

The Z-track method seals the medication deep in the muscle.

Do not massage the site, because that pushes iron back into the tissue.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Iron Dextran (IM)

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Parenteral iron replacement

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 Iron deficiency anemia when oral iron fails

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Skin staining at the site

🔹 Joint aches, fever

🔹 Anaphylaxis (rare but serious)

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Use a large deep muscle like the ventrogluteal

✅ Change the needle after drawing it up

✅ Use Z-track, do not massage

✅ Give a test dose if ordered and watch closely

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Z-track = Zero leak. Pull the skin, inject, wait, release!

photos.question: Which group of findings is classic in a client with severe aortic stenosis?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #344!

❤️ Three symptoms that point straight to a tight heart valve!

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiac question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Chest pain, fainting and breathlessness with exertion

🧠 Rationale: A narrowed aortic valve limits blood flow out of the heart.

During exertion the heart cannot raise its output enough.

This causes angina, syncope and heart failure symptoms.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Aortic Stenosis

❤️ What Happens:

🔹 The aortic valve narrows and stiffens

🔹 The left ventricle works harder and thickens

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Angina

🔹 Syncope

🔹 Dyspnea on exertion

🔹 Harsh systolic murmur at the right second intercostal space

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Teach the client to avoid heavy exertion

✅ Rise slowly, watch for fainting

✅ Monitor for heart failure signs

🚑 When to escalate:

🔹 New fainting, chest pain or worsening shortness of breath

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Aortic stenosis = SAD: Syncope, Angina, Dyspnea!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: A client had a total gastrectomy. Which therapy will the client need for life?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #345!

🍽️ No stomach means one vitamin can no longer be absorbed!

This is a HIGH-YIELD GI question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Vitamin B12 injections

🧠 Rationale: The stomach makes intrinsic factor.

Without intrinsic factor, vitamin B12 cannot be absorbed from food.

Lifelong B12 shots or nasal spray prevent pernicious anemia.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Total Gastrectomy

🔬 Why B12:

🔹 The stomach's parietal cells make intrinsic factor

🔹 Intrinsic factor is needed to absorb B12

⚠️ Signs of B12 Deficiency:

🔹 Fatigue and pallor

🔹 Smooth, red tongue

🔹 Numbness and tingling in hands and feet

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Get B12 injections for life

✅ Eat small, frequent meals

✅ Watch for dumping syndrome

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

No stomach, no intrinsic factor, no B12. Give the shot!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #GI #Gastrectomy #VitaminB12 #PerniciousAnemia #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client with terminal cancer says, "If I can just make it to my grandson's graduation, I'll be ready." Which stage of grief is this?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #346!

🕊️ One sentence tells you exactly which stage of grief this is!

This is a HIGH-YIELD mental health question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Bargaining

🧠 Rationale: Bargaining is trying to make a deal for more time.

It often uses "if" or "just let me" statements.

The nurse listens and supports the client without false hope.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Stages of Grief (Kubler-Ross)

🧠 The 5 Stages:

🔹 Denial: "This can't be happening"

🔹 Anger: "Why me?"

🔹 Bargaining: "If I can just..."

🔹 Depression: deep sadness, withdrawal

🔹 Acceptance: "I'm ready"

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Listen actively and stay present

✅ Allow the client to express feelings

✅ Avoid false reassurance

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Bargaining sounds like a deal: "If... then..."

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #MentalHealth #Grief #EndOfLife #TherapeuticCommunication #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A runner has a temperature of 105°F (40.6°C), hot dry skin and confusion. What is the nurse's priority?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #347!

🔥 Hot, dry and confused after a run? Every second counts!

This is a HIGH-YIELD emergency care question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Begin rapid cooling

🧠 Rationale: These are signs of heat stroke, a medical emergency.

Rapid cooling, like cold water immersion or ice packs, saves brain and organs.

Antipyretics do not work for heat stroke, and a confused client should not drink.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Heat Stroke

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Core temp 104°F (40°C) or higher

🔹 Confusion or seizures

🔹 Hot skin, may be dry

🔹 Fast heart rate

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Call for help and start cooling now

✅ Cold water immersion or ice packs to neck, armpits, groin

✅ Give IV fluids as ordered

✅ Stop cooling at about 102°F (39°C) to avoid shivering

🚑 Emergency:

🔹 Heat stroke can cause organ failure and death

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Heat stroke: cool first, transport second!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Safety #HeatStroke #EmergencyNursing #FirstAid #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: Which pain scale is best for the nurse to use with a 2-year-old after surgery?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #348!

🧸 A toddler can't tell you a number, so how do you measure pain?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — FLACC scale

🧠 Rationale: A 2-year-old cannot reliably self-report pain.

FLACC uses behavior: Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability.

FACES is used starting around age 3, and numeric scales for older children.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Pediatric Pain Scales

📏 Which Scale When:

🔹 FLACC: infants to about age 3 or nonverbal

🔹 Wong-Baker FACES: about age 3 and up

🔹 Numeric 0 to 10: about age 8 and up

⚠️ FLACC Scores:

🔹 Each category 0 to 2

🔹 Total 0 to 10

🔹 Higher score = more pain

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Reassess pain after every intervention

✅ Involve parents in comfort care

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

FLACC = Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Peds #PediatricNursing #PainAssessment #FLACC #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: The nurse fills out an incident report after a client falls. Which action is correct?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #349!

📝 Where does the incident report go? Most students miss this one!

This is a HIGH-YIELD safety and legal question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Do not mention the incident report in the chart

🧠 Rationale: An incident report is an internal quality tool, not part of the medical record.

Chart only the facts of the fall, the assessment and the care given.

Mentioning the report in the chart can make it part of the legal record.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Incident Reports

📋 Purpose:

🔹 Track errors and safety events

🔹 Improve care, not punish staff

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Assess the client first

✅ Notify the provider

✅ Chart objective facts only

✅ File the report, but never reference it in the chart

⚠️ Never:

🔹 Copy it into the chart

🔹 Blame others in writing

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Chart the fall, not the form!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!
